To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) In semi-arid western Nebraska, IS fertigation of N at multiple growth stages is a better N application method for corn production compared to ES fertigation; 2) IS fertigation of 186 kg N ha - 1 resulted in higher corn grain yields, N uptake, and GRN compared to ES fertigated corn; 3) IS fertigation reduced NO3-N leachate compared to the ES application method; 4) IS fertigation increased corn grain yield

in-season subsurface drip irrigation N applications increased grain yield, gross return after N costs, and N uptake compared to a single surface application, and reduced soil NO3-N concentrations in the 0 to 1.5 m depth compared to surface application.
IS N application methods are more effective than ES N application methods in increasing corn yield and reducing environmental impact in SDI systems in semi-arid regions of the United States.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new N fertilizer application method for corn production using SDI in the semi-arid Great Plains.
the effects of subsurface drip irrigated nitrogen (N) fertigation on corn grain yield, total biomass production, and NO3-N leachate in a semi-arid region.
the development and evaluation of a subsurface drip irrigation system for corn production in western Nebraska.

IS N application with SDI is a viable option for corn in the semi-arid Great Plains.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SDI can be used for corn production in western Nebraska, but the IS method is more efficient in N use and reduces NO3-N leachate compared to the ES method.
IS N application is a more efficient method of N application for SDI corn production in the semi-arid Great Plains.
IS fertigation is a more efficient N management strategy than ES fertigation for SDI corn in the semi-arid Great Plains.

SDI systems have the potential to reduce NO3-N losses and increase crop production when N is applied at various corn growth stage compared to a single ES surface application.
